findings.where: Article specimen, the pull quote “Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!” (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The pull quote is set in logo blue. The page uses that same blue for links (the 'Streamlining the PPP Process' lecture title and 'Play again') and for the button, and the palette tile says so: 'wordmark, links, the button'. A whole sentence in the link colour reads as if it could be clicked. The quote is already marked by italic and a larger size, so the blue adds a third emphasis that it doesn't need.
findings.who_objects: Someone reading an article, who has just learned on the same page that blue means a link and may try to click the quote. Also Angélique, who will copy this treatment into every post with a pull quote, so the link colour gets spread over text that isn't a link.

findings.where: Motion sketch heading 'precise, light, quick'; the article specimen's linked lecture title 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge'
findings.fault: The type-pair tile sets the rule: Gelasio for display and reading, Source Sans 3 for 'the nav, buttons, labels and dates only'. The tile breaks it twice. 'precise, light, quick' is a display-size heading set in the sans (semibold, grey), and the lecture title is a document title set in sans bold, next to article headings that are all in Gelasio. Neither of them is a nav item, button, label or date.
findings.who_objects: The layout round and Angélique, who are meant to draw and edit within this tile. The stated rule and the specimens disagree, so they won't know which face a heading or a document title should use, and the two faces will end up mixed across the site.

findings.where: Article specimen heading 'The World's Best…' and the hero lede 'World Bank's' (both widths); the same straight mark in the tile notes ('logo's', 'Georgia's')
findings.fault: Apostrophes are straight typewriter marks ('), while the quotation marks in the same specimen are curly (“ ” and ‘Abundance’). The mismatch shows most in the large serif article heading, where the straight mark sits beside Gelasio's curly quotes.
findings.who_objects: Mark, a lawyer whose articles are meant to read as considered, edited writing, and careful readers at development banks. This specimen is also the model Angélique copies for every post, so the mismatch would carry into all of them.
